Please read /papers/investigations-5/08_theta_observables_newman_dynamics/03_operator_imaginary_time_evolution/01_green_potential_resolvent/continuation-notes/05_TND_OG_B02_RESULTS_AND_MODEL_CHANGE_20261108. Please provide a high level summary of the current research so that we can brainstorm the best paths forward.

Write notes for this session in the brainstorm folder, and record chat history in the chat-histories folder.

I’ll read the continuation note and the project’s established results, then summarize where the research stands and the main choices ahead. I’ll save this session’s notes in the investigation’s brainstorm folder and set up its chat history capture.

The key distinction is already clear: the latest result helps measure the Green quantity reliably near zeros, but it does not yet show that the quantity is small enough to exclude a zero. I’m checking the earlier obstructions so the summary separates that new capability from the remaining mathematical hurdle.

The earlier work rules out two specific shortcuts: uniform linear stability from the stated source/resolvent data, and the tested short-polynomial quadratic certificates. The new logarithmic method avoids those assumptions, but its error bound becomes more demanding at greater height.

This chat’s history capture has also succeeded; it is registered in the investigation’s chat-histories folder.

I’m framing the paths forward around two separate goals: completing the reliable measurement method, and finding an arithmetic reason its value must be small. E03 is the bounded next step for the first goal. For the second, any new idea needs to identify information about the exact theta source that the existing collision controls do not share.

**The research has an exact detector for off-critical-line zeros and a promising way to estimate it reliably. The missing step remains an arithmetic upper bound strong enough to exclude those zeros.**

The central object is the Green potential \(J\), a weighted sum of positive contributions from nonreal zeros of the Newman field. A hypothetical zero in a specified region forces \(J\) above an explicit threshold. The strategy is therefore to obtain an independent upper bound below that threshold. Real zeros—including multiple real zeros—do not contribute interior mass, so this observable addresses location rather than simplicity.

At time zero, \(J\) also equals a localized logarithmic average of zeta, minus an explicit prime sum, plus a pole correction. **The important information lies in that signed difference.** Bounding its pieces separately can lose the cancellation needed for exclusion.

The recent work has established three things:

| Result | What we learned |
|---|---|
| **B01: conditioning obstruction** | Within a specified perturbed-source family, changes of size \(\eta\) in source/resolvent data can produce Green changes of size \(\sqrt{\eta}\). Uniform linear stability fails on that family; theta-specific estimates remain open. |
| **E01/E02: short-polynomial obstruction** | The tested class of short, bounded-coefficient polynomials has a positive average quadratic-residual floor. This limits that particular certificate recipe, without ruling out signed logarithmic estimates or adaptive alternatives. |
| **B02: boundary-log approximation** | The logarithmic integral can be approximated with an explicit error tending to zero, even through multiple real zeros. This avoids requiring a nonzero denominator on the real boundary. |

B02 is the latest constructive advance. Its local proof has proof-author checking only; the research has no independent specialist human review.

**E03 is still unfinished.** It would combine the local logarithmic estimate with the finite source approximation, remote tails and prime truncation into a complete upper approximation. Success would establish reliable acquisition of \(J\). It would still leave open whether the resulting value falls below the zero-detection threshold. Moreover, the error exponent deteriorates with height, so mathematical convergence does not yet establish practical efficiency.

For brainstorming, I would distinguish three paths:

1. **Complete E03 as a bounded analytical result.** The route and completion test are already specified. This would give subsequent research a dependable estimating tool.
2. **Assess practical feasibility before a numerical campaign.** Examine the required precision, source amplification and tail costs. A later small pilot should answer a fixed accuracy/cost question against a comparable direct method.
3. **Focus conceptual work on the missing arithmetic cancellation.** Identify a quantitative feature of the exact theta source that forces the logarithmic average and prime baseline sufficiently close, including exceptional centers and arbitrarily small off-axis distances. Any proposed mechanism must distinguish the known collision controls at the level of its actual inequalities.

My strongest recommendation for our brainstorming is the third question: **what additional arithmetic information could make the true signed value small?** E03 clarifies how to measure that value; this is where a further RH-relevant advance must enter.

I saved the [session notes](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/08_theta_observables_newman_dynamics/03_operator_imaginary_time_evolution/01_green_potential_resolvent/brainstorm/notes/03_TND_OG_RESEARCH_SUMMARY_AND_PATHS_FORWARD_20261108.md) and registered [chat history](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/08_theta_observables_newman_dynamics/03_operator_imaginary_time_evolution/01_green_potential_resolvent/chat-histories/README.md), with final-reply capture queued.

**Next execution: [E] TND-OG-E03 — Sol6.1**, completing the signed-log acquisition proof. It remains unactivated.

Can you first write a draft manuscript with these results? Please focus on analytical results, leaving any numerics for supporting evidence. Please develop the ideas systematically, and methodically derive all of the relevant results, maximizing the coherence of the development of ideas, and the elegance of the results. At the end, describe the outstanding tasks.

I’ll write an evolving manuscript that develops the Green potential, the two scoped obstructions, and the new logarithmic approximation theorem in a coherent analytical sequence. I’ll keep the unfinished E03 assembly distinct from the proved results and end with the outstanding tasks.
You can use the parent folder's manuscript as background

I’ll use the parent manuscript for the source normalization and complete Green identity, then make this draft self-contained around the branch’s results. The development will move from the exact representation, through the stability and quadratic obstructions, to the direct logarithmic estimate.

The proof sources give the draft a clear organizing thread: complete logarithmic data retain the zero signal, while certain stability and quadratic estimates lose too much information. I’ll include the E02 correction explicitly, so the manuscript uses the verified real mixed-term calculation rather than repeating the earlier source-attribution error.

The source, resolvent, Green potential, prime baseline, and square-root obstruction are drafted. I’m now developing the quadratic-residual proof, including its exact polynomial class and padded interval, before the boundary-log theorem. Those hypotheses matter: the obstruction limits one estimation method, not the Green potential itself.

The analytical draft now includes the local logarithmic theorem and its explicit height dependence. Its final section separates five remaining tasks: complete the global error bound, assess the proof, obtain a favorable canonical value, address uniformity and cost, and define any later numerical diagnostic. I’m checking references and compiling the reading copy next.

The draft compiles to 23 pages. I’m checking the equations, attribution and page layout, with particular care to keep the proved local logarithmic estimate separate from the global assembly that remains open.

The checks so far preserve the key conclusions: the square-root conditioning obstruction, the scoped short-mollifier residual floor, and logarithmic approximation through real multiple zeros. I’m recording the source checks and manuscript milestone now; the draft ends with a prioritized list of the remaining analytical tasks.

The manuscript and reading PDF are complete. The final build has no unresolved references or layout warnings, and I’ve inspected all 23 pages. The session notes, source-check record and milestone entries are saved; I’m finishing the chat-history refresh.

Created a **23-page analytical manuscript** with systematic derivations, the corrected mixed-term argument, and a final section on outstanding tasks. It compiles cleanly and has been visually checked.

The global logarithmic assembly and favorable canonical estimate remain explicitly open. Session notes are saved in the brainstorm folder, and chat history has been refreshed.

One question, in a previous discussion we had also considered hierarchies like in investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics. I'm not sure if that made it into the research-overview. Can you check for this relationship and see if there is any relation to the work that could be useful?

I’ll check the earlier hierarchy work and the current research overview, then trace which connections could help with the Green-potential estimates. I’ll save the findings in the brainstorm notes and refresh the chat history.

I found the earlier connection: it is explicit in the parent’s hierarchy locator and the correlation branch’s overview. The Green/resolvent overview only points to that locator for the older Wirtinger formulation, so it does not explain the heat-density connection clearly.

The most promising link is between the hierarchy’s field approximations and the new logarithmic approximation theorem. I’m checking their time ranges and error scales before recommending how to combine them.

There is an important refinement: the strong growing-order recurrence result stops short of time zero, but the later heat-density work does reach time zero with weaker accuracy.

That gives us a useful connection to investigate. A field approximation can feed the one-sided logarithmic estimate without dividing by the field at its zeros. The remaining issue is quantitative: the logarithmic bound becomes less sensitive to improvements in field accuracy as height grows, so a fixed algebraic error rate may not be enough.

The connection is stronger than the old locator suggested. The logarithmic theorem accepts a measurable approximation on the real boundary, so it can use the hierarchy’s higher-order Riemann–Siegel data directly at time zero.

I’ve worked out a local error bound: letting the correction order grow like \(\log\log X\) makes the logarithmic approximation error tend to zero on unit intervals, while retaining all arithmetic modes. This improves approximation control; it does not yet show that the Green potential is small.

I’m recording the connection in the overview and checking the constants and time ranges. The useful conclusion concerns local approximation of the boundary logarithm; obtaining a sufficiently small signed Green value remains a separate task.

The main distinction is now clear: the earlier hierarchy can supply increasingly accurate field approximations, while the new logarithmic estimate makes those approximations usable even across real zeros. The older fluctuation equations also remain relevant, but their covariance term has no automatic sign, so they do not yet provide the required Green bound.

The overview and brainstorm notes now include the relationship and the local derivation. I’m checking the links and research records, with particular care to distinguish the time-zero result from the stronger estimates proved only at negative Newman times.

Yes—partly. The parent’s prior-work notes and the correlation overview explicitly discussed these hierarchies, but the Green overview had only an indirect pointer. I’ve added a substantive connection in [overview §7](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/08_theta_observables_newman_dynamics/03_operator_imaginary_time_evolution/01_green_potential_resolvent/research-overview/01_TND_OG_GREEN_RESOLVENT_RESEARCH_OVERVIEW_20261107.md).

The most useful connection is **controlled field approximation → controlled boundary logarithm**. The earlier work supplies increasingly accurate approximations to the same canonical \(H\). Our current logarithmic estimate can use them even across real zeros, without requiring a lower bound for \(H\).

There is a concrete analytical consequence. Combining the earlier Riemann–Siegel completion with our logarithmic estimate gives, for a sufficiently conservative choice,
\[
K=O(\log\log X)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\text{integrated logarithmic error}=O((\log X)^{-2})
\]
on unit intervals at large height. The gamma factors cancel exactly under our normalization. This uses the existing **time-zero** remainder, rather than extending a negative-time theorem through zero. The imported remainder is [Polymath’s Proposition 6.2](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.12438v2#S6.SS2).

I recorded the derivation in [Note05](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/08_theta_observables_newman_dynamics/03_operator_imaginary_time_evolution/01_green_potential_resolvent/notes/05_TND_OG_B03_HDA_HIERARCHY_LOG_TRANSFER_20261108.md). It has my self-check, not an independent review. The arithmetic sum still contains \(O(\sqrt X)\) terms; practical evaluation costs remain open.

The older mean/fluctuation hierarchy also offers useful guidance, but its covariance contribution has no automatic favorable sign. It does not yet close the Green estimate.

**My assessment:** this is a useful approximation mechanism. The remaining challenge is assembling the complete weighted estimate and proving its actual signed value is sufficiently small.
